Company Description
Alfa-Leasing has been supporting entrepreneurs for over 26 years by designing leasing products that meet the needs of businesses of all sizes across Russia. The company provides passenger and commercial vehicles, trucks, specialized machinery, trailers, semi-trailers, and equipment on flexible leasing terms, including options with a down payment from 0%. Alfa-Leasing focuses on helping clients start generating income from the first day of leasing through convenient, fast service and tailored financial solutions. The organization values strong client partnerships, a collaborative and respectful team culture, accountability for results, and an entrepreneurial mindset that embraces proactive, flexible problem-solving. This environment offers professionals the opportunity to contribute to ambitious goals while continuously improving products and services.

The Vice President Information Technology is a full-time remote role responsible for leading Alfa-Leasing’s overall IT vision and execution. This position oversees the design, implementation, and optimization of IT systems and infrastructure that support leasing operations, client services, and internal business processes. Day-to-day responsibilities include directing IT strategy and architecture, managing IT teams and vendors, prioritizing and delivering technology projects, and ensuring system reliability, security, and regulatory compliance. The role also involves collaborating with executive leadership to align technology initiatives with business goals, driving digital transformation, and monitoring performance metrics to continuously improve efficiency and user experience. The Vice President Information Technology will foster a culture of innovation, risk management, and service excellence within the IT function.

Strong understanding of digital platforms, data management, and integration of enterprise applications.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to collaborate across business units and cultures.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field.
Fluency in English; additional language skills and familiarity with the Russian market are beneficial.

The Company:

Czarnowski Collective is a leading experiential marketing and brand activation company, designing and delivering trade show exhibits, environments, and events for enterprise clients. It's been over 75 years since we opened our doors, but we're still not resting on our reputation or accolades. We're wondering "what if…" — anticipating what's next and building the systems and data platforms that power a business built on forward-thinking work for forward-thinking brands.

Joining the Czarnowski Collective means the opportunity to be more than a number, more than a job title, more than a spectator. We are a collective of dreamers and thinkers, doers, and makers…and we're searching for more of the same to join the ranks.

The Purpose:

We are looking for a Director, IT PMO to join our team in Atlanta! In this role, you'll run governance, budget, vendor, and contract management for Czarnowski Collective's IT project portfolio, chairing the IT Steering Committee and driving executive alignment on priorities and risk across our Microsoft estate — including Dynamics 365 F&O, D365 Sales, Project Operations, and our Power BI/Fabric analytics environment.

This is a hands-on leadership role: rather than delegating our most complex or highest-risk projects, you'll personally lead them while overseeing the broader portfolio through your PMO team. You'll partner closely with the CIO on ERP and digital transformation initiatives, own capex/opex budgeting and forecasting, and be the person who keeps vendors, contracts, and cross-functional stakeholders aligned when priorities and trade-offs get complicated.

You'll build and lead a project management team, set the delivery standards they're held to, and drive the governance and methodology (hybrid agile/waterfall) that keeps ERP, data, and infrastructure projects moving. jobs.title: Internal Audit Executive Director – Global Audit Lead, Cybersecurity, Information Security & Cyber Resilience
jobs.description:
The cyber risk landscape is changing rapidly, and the Firm requires audit leadership equipped to meet the moment. We are seeking an Executive Director to lead internal audit technology coverage across the global Firm and its banking entities, including Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A. (MSBNA) and Morgan Stanley Private Bank, N.A. (MSPBNA). This role demands a forward-looking leader who can address both today's threats and the emerging risks now reshaping cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience — with deep cyber risk expertise and a strong understanding of how artificial intelligence, agentic and frontier AI models, cloud transformation, and digital assets are actively changing the risk landscape and regulatory expectations. The successful candidate will translate these developments into practical, risk-based audit strategies, deliver insightful challenge to management, and evolve the Firm's assurance approach to address current and emerging threats.

The Internal Audit Division (IAD) drives attention and resources to vulnerabilities by providing an independent and well-informed view and impactful messages about the most important risks facing our Firm. This is accomplished by performing a range of assurance activities to independently assess the quality and effectiveness of Morgan Stanley’s system of internal control, including risk management and governance systems and processes. IAD serves as an objective and independent function within the Firm’s risk management framework to foster continual improvement of risk management processes. This is an Executive Director (P6) level position within the Technical Specialist function, which is responsible for providing extensive subject matter expertise and reinforcing the ability of business and technology audit teams to appropriately assess risk and determine and execute coverage.

Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, always evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world.

What You’ll Do In The Role

Prioritize and lead coverage of emerging risks related to artificial intelligence and frontier models — including generative and agentic AI — assessing build time, run time, and life cycle controls, data protection, identity and entitlements for autonomous agents, and the expanded attack surface these capabilities create, as well as adversaries’ growing use of AI to accelerate and scale attacks.
Provide coverage of the idiosyncratic risks arising from cryptocurrency and digital assets, including digital asset custody, private key generation and lifecycle management, and the security of both online (network-connected) and offline (air-gapped) custody infrastructure — highlighting the associated cyber threats such as private key compromise, transaction and address manipulation, smart contract exploitation, and the irreversible loss of assets.
Assess quantum computing and post-quantum cryptography readiness, and other frontier technology risks, ensuring these are reflected in the audit plan and in the Firm’s forward-looking resilience posture.
Monitor the intensifying threat landscape — including advanced attack techniques and regulatory change — and continuously factor emerging threats into audit scoping and assurance coverage.
Provide independent assurance over the design and operating effectiveness of the controls that protect the Firm’s and Banks’ technology environment, customer data, and critical business services
Set and lead the multi-year, risk-based audit strategy for cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience across the Firm and its Banks, spanning the full technology stack (infrastructure, network, platform, application, and data layers) and each business unit to form an integrated, Firm-wide view of control effectiveness, and how cyber threats, information loss, and a cyber attach could affect business lines, critical services, and legal entities across the Firm.
Direct execution of the audit plan across the core cyber and information security domains — identity and access management, endpoint security, network security, data protection, threat detection and response, and vulnerability management.
Lead assurance activities assessing cyber resilience capabilities, including incident response, disaster recovery, business continuity, and third-party/vendor security.
Evaluate compliance with regulatory expectations (e.g., FFIEC, OCC, FDIC, NYDFS, GLBA, RGF, DORA) and industry frameworks (CRI Profile, NIST CSF, ISO 27001).
Oversee root cause analysis on control failures and audit findings, and track remediation to closure.
Comprehensively articulate actionable insights regarding the criticality and impact of cyber risk, and how well it is managed, to senior management and regulators. Prepare materials for the Chief Audit Executive’s updates to the Audit Committee and the Board,
Coordinate with second-line risk and compliance functions and with external auditors and regulators, and collaborate with global peers to identify risk themes and implications across business segments and legal entities.
Mentor and develop audit staff and manage a global team; help inform and address talent needs and identify stretch and development opportunities for team members.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

Advanced understanding of cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience risks and the relevant regulations, including banking regulatory requirements.
Experience assessing emerging technology risks and their control implications — including AI and agentic AI, frontier models, cryptocurrency and digital asset custody, and quantum/post-quantum cryptography — and the ability to translate a rapidly changing threat landscape into practical audit coverage.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CRI Profile) and experience auditing identity and access management, cloud security, and network architecture.
Expertise in audit principles, methodology, tools, and processes (e.g., risk assessments, planning, testing, reporting, and continuous monitoring).
Ability to analyze data and prioritize coverage and assurance activities based on the criticality of risk.
Ability to articulate risk and impact clearly and succinctly to different audiences, including senior stakeholders, the Board, and regulators.
Ability to inspire and support others to do their best work through active coaching, feedback, and development opportunities, and by ensuring trust and inclusion among team members.
Experience in overseeing resource utilization and monitoring progress against deliverables.
A bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Computer Science, or a related field.
At least 12-15 years’ relevant experience in IT/cyber audit, information security, or risk management — ideally in banking or financial services — would generally be expected to fulfill the skills required for this role.
Relevant certifications (e.g., CISA, CISSP, CISM, or equivalent) preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with incident response or red team/penetration testing programs.
Familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
Prior experience at a large financial institution or a Big 4 consulting firm.

Our values — putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back — aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what’s best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. Lead technical architecture design sessions directly with clients, translating business, security, and compliance requirements into scalable IGA target-state architectures.
Architect and oversee end-to-end implementation of Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) solutions using SailPoint and Saviynt as primary platforms.
Design and lead delivery of core IGA capabilities, including identity lifecycle management (Joiner/Mover/Leaver), access certification/attestation campaigns, role-based access control (RBAC) and role mining, Segregation of Duties (SoD) policy design, entitlement management, and access request/approval workflows.
Lead application onboarding strategy for IGA platforms, including source/target connector design, birthright and non-birthright provisioning, and integration with authoritative HR sources
Define and implement IGA governance frameworks, including policy design, audit and compliance reporting, and global configuration/data segmentation best practices.
Working knowledge of adjacent IAM domains – Privileged Access Management (PAM, e.g., CyberArk, Delinea) and Access Management (SSO/MFA via Entra ID, Okta, Ping) – to ensure IGA architectures integrate cleanly across the broader identity ecosystem.
Own end-to-end delivery for engagements, managing scope, timelines, technical quality, and client satisfaction.
Serve as the primary technical point of contact for clients, running architecture workshops, discovery sessions, and executive-level readouts.
Develop maturity assessments, governance roadmaps, and target operating models tailored to client environments and industry (e.g., healthcare, higher education, financial services).
Provide technical leadership, mentorship, and career development to IAM engineers, architects, and consultants on the delivery team.
Partner with sales and account teams on business development activities, including solution scoping, proposal/SOW development, and technical presentations for prospective clients.
Advise clients on regulatory and compliance considerations (e.g., SOX, HIPAA, GDPR) as they relate to identity governance controls, certifications, and audits.
Monitor emerging IGA trends and best practices (including AI-driven governance) and champion their adoption across client engagements.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field.
10+ years of hands-on IAM experience with a strong concentration in Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), including consulting or client-facing delivery, and at least 3-5 years in a technical leadership or architecture role.
Deep, hands-on expertise architecting and implementing SailPoint and Saviynt, including certification campaigns, RBAC/SoD design, connector configuration, and workflow customization.
Strong understanding of identity lifecycle management, entitlement governance, access certification processes, and provisioning/de-provisioning across enterprise applications.
Working knowledge of PAM concepts and platforms (e.g., CyberArk, Delinea, BeyondTrust) and Access Management/SSO technologies (e.g., Entra ID, Okta, Ping) sufficient to architect integrated IAM solutions.

Experience managing project resources, timelines, and deliverables across multiple concurrent engagements.
Demonstrated experience mentoring and developing technical teams, with strong people leadership skills.
Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts for both technical and executive audiences.

While technical credibility is important, the role is not intended to personally perform all engineering, administration, or support work. Lead technical architecture design sessions directly with clients, translating business, security, and compliance requirements into scalable IGA target-state architectures.
Architect and oversee end-to-end implementation of Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) solutions using SailPoint and Saviynt as primary platforms.

Lead application onboarding strategy for IGA platforms, including source/target connector design, birthright and non-birthright provisioning, and integration with authoritative HR sources

Own end-to-end delivery for engagements, managing scope, timelines, technical quality, and client satisfaction.
Serve as the primary technical point of contact for clients, running architecture workshops, discovery sessions, and executive-level readouts.
Develop maturity assessments, governance roadmaps, and target operating models tailored to client environments and industry (e.g., healthcare, higher education, financial services).
Provide technical leadership, mentorship, and career development to IAM engineers, architects, and consultants on the delivery team.
Partner with sales and account teams on business development activities, including solution scoping, proposal/SOW development, and technical presentations for prospective clients.
Advise clients on regulatory and compliance considerations (e.g., SOX, HIPAA, GDPR) as they relate to identity governance controls, certifications, and audits.
Monitor emerging IGA trends and best practices (including AI-driven governance) and champion their adoption across client engagements.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related field.
10+ years of hands-on IAM experience with a strong concentration in Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), including consulting or client-facing delivery, and at least 3-5 years in a technical leadership or architecture role.
Deep, hands-on expertise architecting and implementing SailPoint and Saviynt, including certification campaigns, RBAC/SoD design, connector configuration, and workflow customization.

Demonstrated experience mentoring and developing technical teams, with strong people leadership skills.

We strongly encourage people of color, transgender and non-binary people to apply. HRC is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes everyone, including non-LGBTQ+ people, to join our team. Don’t meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that people from marginalized communities are less likely to apply for jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At HRC, we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Position Summary

The Human Rights Campaign is a large, national nonprofit civil rights and advocacy organization working to advance equality for LGBTQ+ people. Technology is essential to that work. It enables our staff to organize, advocate, collaborate, and work effectively with partners, volunteers, and communities nationwide.

As Director, IT Operations, you will lead the technology environment that makes that work possible: secure, reliable, well-managed, and easy to use. Reporting to the VP of IT & Data Analytics, who leads enterprise technology strategy and digital transformation, you will serve as HRC’s technical and IT operations leader. You will translate strategy into a practical technology roadmap and lead IT operations, service delivery, enterprise systems, workplace and event technology, operational security, the internal IT team, and our managed service and technology partners.

This is a broad, hands-on operational leadership role in a lean nonprofit setting, not an infrastructure specialty. Success in this role requires balancing strategy, service delivery, vendor management, operational leadership, and technical decision-making. While technical credibility is important, the role is not intended to personally perform all engineering, administration, or support work. Instead, the Director is responsible for ensuring successful outcomes through a combination of internal staff, managed service partners, and other technology vendors.

We are looking for a leader who combines technical credibility with strong people leadership, clear communication, sound judgment, and a commitment to excellent service.

You will build trusted relationships with business owners and internal stakeholders, help teams navigate technology and process changes, simplify and modernize our technology environment, strengthen the IT team and its operating practices, and ensure technology effectively supports HRC’s mission.

Position Responsibilities:

IT Leadership & Modernization
Develop and execute an IT operations and modernization roadmap aligned with organizational priorities, informed by strong partnerships with program owners and internal stakeholders.
Serve as the senior technical advisor for IT operations, evaluating technical options, dependencies, risks, and vendor recommendations.
Lead efforts to simplify legacy and overlapping technologies and advance a secure, cloud-first operating environment.

IT Operations & Service Delivery
Lead day-to-day IT operations across identity and access, endpoints, cloud and infrastructure, productivity and collaboration platforms, and IT-managed enterprise applications.
Ensure effective delivery of technology services through a combination of internal staff, managed service providers, security partners, and technology vendors, establishing clear ownership, accountability, and service expectations.
Establish and mature IT service management practices, including incident, problem, change, knowledge, and asset management, with clear service standards, accountability, and governance. Ensure technology changes are communicated, documented, and managed to reduce operational risk and improve coordination across internal teams and technology partners.
Drive root-cause analysis and durable resolution of recurring technical and service issues.
Lead technical planning and execution for migrations, integrations, upgrades, consolidation, and retirement of legacy technologies.
Ensure technology services are secure, reliable, and operationally ready, including appropriate lifecycle management, patching, backup, and disaster recovery.
Ensure reliable technology and AV support for hybrid meetings, Board meetings, and major organizational events through appropriate planning, resourcing, thorough testing, and coordination of internal and external support resources, providing hands-on support when necessary.

Vendor Management & Cybersecurity
Serve as the primary owner of managed service and key technology partner relationships, establishing clear service expectations, governance processes, reporting, escalation paths, and accountability for outcomes.
Evaluate vendor performance, service quality, and value realization, making recommendations regarding service improvements, scope changes, or provider transitions when appropriate.
Manage IT contracts, licensing, renewals, and technology operating expenditures within approved budgets.
Partner with fractional CISO and cybersecurity service providers to operationalize security controls, incident response, vulnerability remediation, data protection, and risk-reduction priorities.

People Leadership & Communication
Lead, coach, and develop the internal IT team, setting clear expectations for ownership, technical quality, communication, customer service, and follow-through.
Assess team capabilities and recommend appropriate staffing, role design, training, and use of external expertise.
Communicate technical issues, risks, options, and changes clearly to staff, leadership, and non-technical stakeholders to reduce change management challenges

Perform other related duties as required to support organizational operations, major initiatives, and events.

Position Qualifications:

At least 10+ years of progressive IT experience, including 5+ years managing IT operations, service delivery, or comparable enterprise technology functions.
Demonstrated leadership experience managing across multiple IT domains, including identity and access, endpoint management, cloud/infrastructure, enterprise applications, and end-user technology services.
Strong working knowledge of modern identity and endpoint management, including experience supporting both Windows and macOS environments.
Experience managing cloud-based productivity, collaboration, and SaaS environments, including Microsoft 365 and/or Google Workspace.
Strong IT service management experience, particularly incident, problem, change, knowledge, and asset management, with demonstrated success improving service quality and resolving recurring issues.
Proven experience managing MSPs and technology vendors, including service levels, escalations, root-cause analysis, remediation, contracts, and performance accountability.
Experience working with cybersecurity teams or providers to implement security requirements and address operational risks, including identity and endpoint security, vulnerability remediation, incident response, and data protection.
Demonstrated experience managing and developing IT staff, setting clear expectations, building accountability, and improving team performance.
Experience implementing technology roadmaps and managing complex migrations, modernization efforts, or other significant technology initiatives, including stakeholder engagement, communication, and organizational adoption.
Strong technical judgment and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to assess cross-platform issues, identify root causes, evaluate technical recommendations and tradeoffs, and make sound technical decisions.
Ability to build trusted relationships with senior management on technical options, risks, dependencies, and operational implications to inform technology planning, prioritization, and investment decisions.
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to explain technical issues, risks, decisions, and expectations clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to balance hands-on technical involvement with staff management, delegation, vendor oversight, operational priorities, and longer-term initiatives in a lean IT organization.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience modernizing complex or hybrid environments toward simplified, cloud-based services.
Familiarity with Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, Azure, AWS, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, or comparable technologies.
Familiarity with recognized cybersecurity frameworks such as NIST CSF or CIS Controls.
Experience supporting distributed workforces and external stakeholders such as contractors, volunteers, or partners.
Experience in nonprofit, advocacy, or other mission-driven organizations.
Knowledge of or interest in LGBTQ+ issues, and a demonstrated commitment to a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace.

Work Environment & Availability

This position is located at HRC Headquarters in Washington, DC, and requires regular on-site presence of at least four days per week. The role is generally performed during standard business hours but requires flexibility to support organizational events, critical system needs, and operational priorities that may occur in the evenings, on weekends, or on holidays. While the Director is expected to be available for significant incidents and major organizational events, day-to-day operational coverage is shared across internal staff, managed service providers, and established support processes.

All positions at the Human Rights Campaign and/or the Human Rights Campaign Foundation may require regular or periodic travel. Where business travel is required, appropriate compensation as outlined by the Fair Labor Standards Act will apply.

Employer is the Human Rights Campaign, Inc., an I.R.C. 501(c)(4) non-profit entity.

No phone calls or emails, please. Due to the volume of applications we receive, we are unable to respond to queries about application status.

new_jobs.description:
Alignment Health is breaking the mold in conventional health care, committed to serving seniors and those who need it most: the chronically ill and frail. It takes an entire team of passionate and caring people, united in our mission to put the senior first. We have built a team of talented and experienced people who are passionate about transforming the lives of the seniors we serve. In this fast-growing company, you will find ample room for growth and innovation alongside the Alignment Health community. Working at Alignment Health provides an opportunity to do work that really matters, not only changing lives but saving them. Together.

The Senior Director, Chief of Staff & Portfolio Management serves as the strategic operating partner to the Chief Digital Officer, translating digital vision into disciplined execution across a complex Medicare Advantage technology and operations portfolio. This role works directly with the CDO, executive leadership team, clinical, finance, compliance, and operational stakeholders to align priorities, govern investments, and drive outcomes across the organization's most critical digital programs. The role owns the Technology portfolio program management function — including project management, performance reporting, and initiative execution — and serves as the senior accountability point for organizational operating rhythms and cross-functional program delivery. Success is measured by the health and pace of technology initiatives, quality of executive decision-making support, and the maturity of portfolio governance practices across the Technology function.

Job Duties / Responsibilities

Advise and Enable CDO Decision-Making.

Partner with the CDO as a primary strategic thought partner — synthesizing data, preparing executive communications, and coordinating leadership priorities to accelerate informed decisions.

Lead Technology Portfolio Governance.

Own the portfolio management function, including initiative intake, prioritization, governance frameworks, and status reporting, to ensure investments stay aligned with technology and organizational strategy.

Drive Cross-Functional Program Execution.

Direct the execution of complex, cross-functional initiatives spanning technology, clinical operations, regulatory compliance, and business functions, resolving blockers and maintaining delivery momentum.

Govern Technology Investment & Capital Planning.

Manage the annual and multi-year technology investment planning process in partnership with Technology, Finance, and business leaders, while building tooling and processes to track spend performance, value realization, and build-versus-buy decisions.

Establish and Drive Operating Rhythms.

Build and maintain the CDO organization's operating cadences — leadership meetings, governance forums, planning cycles — fostering accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement.

Deliver Executive Performance Reporting.

Develop and manage scorecards, KPIs, and operational dashboards that provide the CDO, CEO, and Board Committees with timely visibility into portfolio health, risks, and decision requirements.

Lead Organizational Effectiveness Initiatives.

Support operating model adoption, transformation programs, and execution maturity improvements that strengthen how the digital organization delivers at scale in a Medicare Advantage regulated environment.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Fulfill supervisory responsibilities in accordance with organization policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.

Experience

Required:

8–12 years of progressive experience in digital strategy, program management, technology portfolio governance, or a related strategic operations function
3+ years of experience in a healthcare payer, managed care, or Medicare Advantage environment, with demonstrated understanding of CMS regulatory requirements, HIPAA compliance, and health plan operations
Demonstrated experience leading and governing complex, cross-functional technology or digital portfolios with measurable outcomes
Proven track record as a strategic advisor or operating partner to C-suite or senior executive leaders, including preparation of board-level communications and executive decision support
Experience establishing and operationalizing PMO governance frameworks, portfolio management methodologies, and organizational operating cadences

Preferred:

Prior experience in a Chief of Staff, Strategy & Operations Director, or Senior Program Director role supporting a CDO, CTO, or equivalent digital executive in a health insurance or health technology organization
Experience leading operating model transformation or product-centric organizational adoption in a regulated healthcare environment
Background in Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent process improvement and operational excellence disciplines

Education

Required:

Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Information Technology, Healthcare Administration, Health Informatics, or a related field; 4 years of additional relevant experience may be considered in lieu of a degree

Preferred:

Master's degree (MBA, MHA, MIS, or equivalent) with a focus on strategy, operations, or healthcare management

Training

Familiarity with structured program and project management methodologies (e.g., PMI/PMP, Agile, SAFe, or equivalent); formal training or applied experience is acceptable
Working knowledge of HIPAA compliance requirements and CMS regulatory frameworks applicable to Medicare Advantage plan operations

Preferred:

Project Management Professional (PMP) certification or equivalent portfolio/program management credential
Agile or SAFe certification (e.g., SAFe Program Consultant, Certified Scrum Master) where applicable to the delivery model

Skills & Competencies

Technical / Role-Specific Skills

Ability to design and operate governance structures, manage multi-initiative portfolios, and ensure strategic alignment, investment discipline, and delivery accountability at scale.

Executive Communication & Stakeholder Influence

Proven ability to build board-ready materials, translate complex technology portfolios into business narratives, and influence senior leaders across technology, clinical, finance, and compliance functions.

Digital Strategy & Operating Model Design

Deep understanding of digital transformation principles, product-centric operating models, and the organizational changes required to sustain them in a regulated Medicare Advantage environment.

Medicare Advantage / Healthcare Payer Domain Knowledge

Working knowledge of Medicare Advantage plan operations, CMS regulations, Stars programs, risk adjustment, and HIPAA compliance as they relate to digital and technology initiatives.

Performance Measurement & Executive Reporting

Ability to build and maintain scorecards, KPIs, and dashboards that provide actionable visibility into portfolio health, organizational risk, and strategic initiative performance.

Cross-Functional Program Execution

Demonstrated ability to orchestrate delivery across vendor partners, product teams, engineering, clinical operations, and business units in a complex, matrixed organization.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Chief Technology Officer is responsible for setting and executing the company’s technology vision, owning the full engineering and platform stack, and ensuring that technology decisions directly accelerate business outcomes, product innovation, and go to market performance. The CTO reports to the Chief Executive Officer and leads a team of 50 or more across software engineering, data integrations, infrastructure and Cloud, and testing. The CTO is a senior executive partner who thinks commercially, communicates transparently, and builds world class teams.

The CTO will be a key contributor to company strategy, client success, and Strategic Partner relations, and will represent engineering at the executive level. The right candidate combines deep technical depth with sharp business acumen, understands the unique dynamics of higher education institutions, and has a demonstrated record of building and scaling SaaS platforms in a high growth environment.

Additionally, the CTO will work with other parts of the organization in cross-company initiatives, such as corporate security, AI transformation, and corporate policy governance. He/she will have high levels of passion, intellect, drive, and energy and will be a self-confident, team-oriented individual with strong ethics and integrity.

Strategic Planning and Vision

The CTO shapes and champions the technology strategy that powers Ad Astra’s mission, product evolution, and competitive differentiation in the higher education market.

Team Leadership

The CTO builds and sustains a high performing engineering organization rooted in accountability, psychological safety, and a culture of continuous improvement.

Software Development

The CTO owns the engineering processes, quality standards, and delivery mechanisms that power Ad Astra’s SaaS platform. The CTO drives a modern, discipline-driven software development lifecycle grounded in Agile principles and SVPG product practices.

Artificial Intelligence, Data, and Analytics

The CTO leads Ad Astra’s evolution as an AI enabled, data driven platform company, ensuring that data architecture, data science capability, and AI strategy are first class investments deeply integrated into the product roadmap and business strategy.

Infrastructure & Security

The CTO is accountable for a resilient, scalable, and secure cloud infrastructure that meets the reliability expectations of higher education institutions and the compliance requirements of regulated data environments.

Minimum of 15 years of progressive technology experience, with at least 10 years leading engineering organizations within B2B SaaS companies serving mid-market or enterprise clients.

Strong background in data engineering, data integration architecture, and enterprise data platform design using modern cloud data tools.
Experience operating within or alongside a private equity-backed environment, with an understanding of the performance expectations, operational cadence, and value creation priorities of PE ownership.

Company

At BioCryst, we share a deep commitment to improving the lives of people living with hereditary angioedema (HAE) and other rare diseases. We leverage our expertise in structure-guided drug design to develop first-in-class or best-in-class oral small-molecule and injectable protein therapeutics. Our global headquarters is in Durham, North Carolina, we have a regional office in Boston, Massachusetts, and our employees span the globe across sites in multiple countries. We are proud of our culture of engagement and accountability that rewards people for innovative thinking and achievement of key objectives. For more information, please visit our website at www.biocryst.com or follow us   on LinkedIn and Instagram .

Job Summary

BioCryst is a fast-growing pharmaceutical company seeking an experienced Associate Director, IT Business - Partner Pharmaceutical Development to build and mature strategic partnerships across Development. The role supports Program & Portfolio Management, Clinical Development / Operations, Biometrics, Pharmacology / Non-Clinical, Regulatory, Safety, and Medical Affairs. The IT Business Partner will understand functional strategies and operating needs, translate them into technology roadmaps and prioritized initiatives, and enable compliant, scalable process and system improvements across the development lifecycle. This role serves as a strategic technology advisor and delivery leader, with responsibility for business analysis, program and project leadership, solution design, data and integration strategy, vendor management, adoption, and ongoing application support. The role requires working knowledge of key Development platforms and capabilities, including Veeva RIM, Veeva CTMS, ReadCube, clinical data visualization and analytics solutions, and the Oracle Argus safety system. Please note: this role can be remote working east coast with a strong preference for the Boston, MA area.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Serve as the primary IT Business Partner and trusted technology advisor for Program & Portfolio Management, Clinical Development / Operations, Biometrics, Pharmacology / Non-Clinical, Regulatory, Safety, and Medical Affairs.
Build strong partnerships with functional leaders and subject matter experts to understand strategies, business capabilities, pain points, risks, and priorities.
Translate business priorities into multi-year technology roadmaps, business cases, demand plans, and sequenced delivery portfolios.
Lead demand intake, discovery, requirements definition, solution evaluation, prioritization, implementation, adoption, and value realization for Development technology initiatives.
Provide subject matter expertise for the selection, implementation, enhancement, integration, and support of Development applications and data capabilities.
Partner with business and IT stakeholders to optimize platforms including Veeva RIM, Veeva CTMS, ReadCube, clinical data visualization and analytics solutions, Oracle Argus, and related Development systems.
Develop a working understanding of Development processes and data flows, including clinical study operations, regulatory information and submissions, safety and pharmacovigilance, biometrics, non-clinical activities, processes, and medical information or evidence-generation needs.
Collaborate with Enterprise Architecture, Data and Analytics, Information Security, Infrastructure, Integration, and IT Compliance teams to design scalable, secure, reliable, and supportable solutions.
Ensure GxP and other regulated applications are implemented and maintained in accordance with applicable validation, data integrity, privacy, security, change control, and records-management requirements.
Oversee system lifecycle activities, including application ownership, release management, vendor upgrades, incident and problem management, access governance, business continuity, disaster recovery, and application retirement.
Promote consistent master data, system interoperability, and integrated data flows across internal platforms, CROs, service providers, and other Development partners.
Partner with Clinical, Biometrics, and Data and Analytics teams to improve access to trusted study information and strengthen clinical data visualization, reporting, and decision support.
Lead cross-functional programs and projects, managing scope, schedule, budget, resources, risks, dependencies, decisions, communications, and executive-level status reporting.
Manage strategic technology vendors and managed service providers, including performance, service levels, delivery quality, contracts, and issue escalation.
Drive user adoption through stakeholder engagement, communications, training, process documentation, and change-management activities.
Monitor emerging technologies, including automation, analytics, and responsible AI, and recommend practical opportunities that support Development priorities and compliance expectations.
This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports. The role leads and manages MSPs, contractors, vendors, and consultants, as needed, for project implementation, project delivery, and ongoing system support.
Contribute to IT standards, policies, procedures, governance practices, and continuous-improvement efforts.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Experience & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science, business, life sciences, or a related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
At least 8–10 years of progressive experience delivering and managing information technologies and services in a corporate environment, preferably in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or broader life sciences industry.
Demonstrated experience as an IT Business Partner, product owner, application leader, program manager, or similar role supporting Development or R&D business functions.
Strong knowledge of business processes and information needs across several of the following areas: Program & Portfolio Management, Clinical Development / Operations, Biometrics, Pharmacology / Non-Clinical, Regulatory, Safety, and Medical Affairs.
Experience in managing, enhancing, integrating, or supporting Veeva RIM and Veeva CTMS or comparable regulatory and clinical platforms.
Knowledge of Oracle Argus or a comparable pharmacovigilance and safety system.
Knowledge of SAS (LSAF) and A2Ai
Knowledge of ReadCube or comparable scientific literature and reference-management solutions.
Knowledge of clinical data sources, standards, reporting, and visualization approaches used to support study oversight and Development decision-making.
Experience with regulated GxP computerized systems, including validation, data integrity, audit trails, electronic records and signatures, security, change control, and inspection readiness.
Experience leading application implementations and lifecycle management in cloud-based, client-server, and web-based environments.
Experience with system integrations, data flows, vendor-hosted platforms, and external partners such as CROs and managed service providers.
Strong business analysis, process-improvement, solution-evaluation, program and project management, resource planning, and vendor-management skills.
Demonstrated ability to develop technology roadmaps, investment proposals, implementation plans, operating models, and measurable outcomes.
Experience leading contractors, and external partners in a matrixed and cross-functional environment.
Strong interpersonal, written, verbal, facilitation, and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with business leaders, technical teams, end users, and vendors.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, navigate ambiguity, influence without direct authority, and work effectively both as a leader and as a contributing team member.
